questions.question: Why is raw Monte Carlo return a difficult signal for policy updates?
options: It has high variance from episode to episode
It cannot be computed unless the environment is deterministic
It always underestimates long-term reward
It only works for discrete actions
questions.explanation: The lesson opens by stressing that REINFORCE is noisy because full returns can vary dramatically across episodes. Multiplying those noisy returns by log-policy gradients leads to slow, high-variance learning.

questions.question: What intuitive role does a baseline play in policy-gradient methods?
options: It forces the policy to be deterministic
It gives the agent a comparison point for whether an action did better or worse than expected
It replaces the need for rewards
It makes the method off-policy
questions.explanation: A baseline lets the agent compare observed outcomes against what was expected from the state. This is exactly the intuition behind advantage: actions are judged by whether they were above or below average for that state.

questions.question: In actor-critic, what are the actor and critic responsible for?
options: The actor estimates returns and the critic samples actions
The actor stores replay data and the critic clips rewards
The actor outputs the policy and the critic estimates state value
The actor computes entropy and the critic computes KL divergence
questions.explanation: The lesson defines the actor as pi_theta(a|s), the policy used to act, and the critic as V_phi(s), the value estimator trained by regression. The critic supplies a lower-variance learning signal to the actor.

questions.question: Which expression is the one-step TD advantage used in actor-critic?
options: G_t - V(s_t)
r_{t+1} + gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t)
log pi(a_t|s_t) - V(s_t)
questions.explanation: The lesson names the TD-residual advantage as delta_t = r_{t+1} + gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t). It is biased because it uses the learned value function, but it usually has much lower variance than Monte Carlo advantage.

questions.question: What is the main practical difference between A2C and A3C in the lesson?
options: A2C is off-policy while A3C is on-policy
A2C uses synchronous batched environments, while A3C uses asynchronous worker threads updating shared parameters
A2C has no critic, while A3C has a critic
A2C requires replay buffers, while A3C requires target networks
questions.explanation: A2C collects rollouts synchronously across parallel environments and updates on a combined batch. A3C instead runs multiple workers asynchronously and lets them push gradients to shared parameters, which was important for CPU-scale training.
